title: Cross-functional Governance Playbook — Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendors, Travel, Templates
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary

This playbook consolidates company-wide policies and step-by-step processes for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor lifecycle, travel policy, and reusable internal templates. It is intended for team leads, people-ops, finance, security, and engineering managers who coordinate cross-functional approvals and operational setup.

Key principles
- Least privilege by default: grant minimal access necessary and review quarterly.
- Clear separation of duties: approval, execution, and review must be distinct where risk is material.
- Auditability: every access grant, change, purchase, and vendor decision must have an auditable ticket or record.
- Risk-based controls: apply stricter controls to confidential data, infrastructure, or supplier relationships.

1) Access & Permissions (RBAC and exceptions)
Overview: All service accounts, console access, and data store roles follow the RBAC baseline defined below. Exceptions require documented business justification and timeboxed approvals.

- RBAC Baseline (applies to cloud consoles, internal admin panels, databases, and monitoring tools):
  - Viewer: read-only access for general staff (SLO: review period 90 days)
  - Developer: code, deploy with guarded permissions; no billing or org admin
  - SRE/Infra: deployment + alerting + incident-run permissions; no billing admin by default
  - Security/Compliance: audit-read across systems; escalate changes where required
  - Billing/Finance: billing console access only for designated finance members

- Access request flow (typical):
  1. Requestor opens an access request ticket in our ITSM tool (ticket template: "access-request") and selects resource + justification.
  2. Requestor’s manager approves in the ticket.
  3. Owning team (service owner) approves and assigns expiration (default 30 days for elevated privileges).
  4. Identity team applies role via IAM and links ticket ID to the change.
  5. After expiration, a reminder goes to manager; the request is either renewed or revoked.

- Emergency access (break-glass):
  - Process: Pager duty alert → SRE lead gives temporary token for max 4 hours → after-action report submitted within 24 hours.
  - Owner: Eng-SRE.

- Quarterly access review: team leads receive a report and must certify users and service accounts. Non-responses default to suspension after 14 days.

2) Change Management (infra, runtime, and config changes)
Purpose: Ensure predictable rollouts and minimize outages. Applies to infra-as-code, runtime config, model serving config, and tenant-routing policy changes.

- Change categories and approval matrix (text table):
  - Low-risk (non-prod config, documentation): Auto-approve via CI (owner approval).
  - Medium-risk (prod config toggles, scaling rules): Team owner + SRE review required.
  - High-risk (production schema changes, model rollout, network or firewall changes): Team owner + Eng-SRE + Security sign-off; scheduled maintenance window; post-deploy verification.

- Change lifecycle (numbered steps):
  1. Create change ticket with scope, rollback plan, and test matrix. Include canary strategy if applicable.
  2. Automated CI checks: linting, unit/integration tests, and deployment dry-run.
  3. Approval step(s) from matrix above.
  4. Schedule change during designated windows (unless emergency).
  5. Execute with telemetry enabled; monitor SLOs for 30 minutes post-deploy.
  6. Close ticket with postmortem if any anomaly observed.

- Rollback criteria (examples):
  - Error rate > 1% absolute increase for 5 minutes on key endpoints.
  - 95th latency exceeds SLA by 2x for 3 consecutive minutes.

- Example gitops checklist snippet:
  ```yaml
  change_ticket: CHG-{{ID}}
  owner: teams/serving-runtime
  canary: true
  rollback_plan: revert-commit {{SHA}}
  monitors: [tokens-per-second, tail-latency-p95, error-rate]
  ```

3) Data Management (classification, handling, retention)
Policy summary: Data is classified into PUBLIC, INTERNAL, CONFIDENTIAL, and RESTRICTED. Handling, access, encryption, and retention vary by class.

- Classification & rules (short):
  - PUBLIC: OK to publish. No special handling.
  - INTERNAL: Company-internal, minimal restrictions, accessible to employees.
  - CONFIDENTIAL: Customer data, contracts, PII; encryption at rest + in transit; access via RBAC; audit logging enabled.
  - RESTRICTED: Regulated data (HIPAA, PCI, regulated financial data). Requires additional controls, formal Data Processing Addendum (DPA), and may be restricted to Private deployments.

- Data retention & deletion:
  - Default data retention for logs: 90 days (short-term), aggregated metrics retained 2 years.
  - Customer PII: retention per contract; default 1 year after contract termination unless otherwise required.
  - Retention change procedure: Data owner opens request, legal reviews, security approves, and infra executes purge.

- Data access audit: Quarterly automated reports include who accessed confidential stores and which keys were used. Alerts for unusual bulk exports.

- Example: Granting analytics access to a dataset (procedure):
  1. Create dataset request and attach business case + columns required.
  2. Data owner approves minimal column set and mask rules.
  3. Security performs a quick PET (privacy engineering test).
  4. Identity team grants role-limited access scoped to dataset and duration.

4) Procurement & Expenses (thresholds, PO, card usage)
Objective: Streamline purchases while maintaining controls for spend and vendor risk.

- Spend thresholds & approval authorities:
  - <= $2,000: Approver = Requester’s manager (expense card or non-PO).
  - $2,001 — $25,000: Department head + Finance review (PO required).
  - > $25,000: VP-level approval + Finance + Legal, contract review mandatory.

- Purchase process (steps):
  1. Requester completes purchase request template (link to template at bottom) including cost center, budget owner, and business justification.
  2. Finance verifies budget availability and issues PO if required.
  3. Vendor sends invoice referencing PO; Finance reconciles and schedules payment net-30 unless otherwise agreed.

- Corporate card usage: personal expenses prohibited. Cardholders must submit receipts within 7 days and code charges to cost centers. Monthly audits run by Finance.

- Reimbursement process (travel & expenses):
  - Submit via expense system with scanned receipts and policy code. Payroll/Finance issues reimbursement next payroll cycle or per Finance SLA (14 days).

5) Vendor Management & Onboarding
Goal: Evaluate vendor risk, ensure contractual protections, and define operational points-of-contact.

- Vendor risk tiers and controls (text list):
  - Low-risk (SaaS subscriptions without customer data): Standard SOW, Finance PO.
  - Medium-risk (vendors with access to internal systems or non-sensitive customer data): Security review + SOC2 or equivalent required.
  - High-risk (process confidential or regulated customer data, access to infra): Legal + Security + Exec review; Data Processing Agreement and security questionnaire mandatory.

- Onboarding checklist (ordered steps):
  1. Business sponsor fills vendor intake form.
  2. Finance confirms procurement route and budget.
  3. Security runs the vendor security questionnaire and requests evidence (SOC2, pen test reports).
  4. Legal negotiates the contract and DPA.
  5. IT creates accounts/network rules and issues the ticket to the owning team for final verification.
  6. Tag vendor record in vendor registry with renewal/cancellation dates.

- Performance & SLA monitoring: Vendors with SLAs must be instrumented into the vendor dashboard with monthly health reviews. Non-compliant vendors trigger remediation; persistent issues escalate to procurement lead for renegotiation or termination.

6) Travel Policy (booking, per diem, approvals, safety)
Principles: Safety first, reasonable economy, and cost-conscious travel.

- Booking rules:
  - Use corporate travel portal for air and hotels when available. Book at least 7 days in advance for domestic travel where possible.
  - Economy or premium economy for flights under 6 hours. Business class requires VP approval or if medical necessity documented.

- Per diem & allowed items:
  - Domestic: $75/day for meals (including tips).
  - International: Country-specific per diem; default $125/day unless finance publishes a different rate.
  - Excess charges (entertainment, client dinners) require pre-approval and itemized receipts.

- Safety and incident reporting: Employees must register travel in the company travel tracker and report any safety incidents to People Ops within 24 hours.

- Expense submission timeline: Submit receipts within 7 days of trip completion. Late submissions beyond 45 days may be denied unless pre-authorized.

7) Internal Templates (where to find and how to use)
This playbook includes or links to canonical templates for common requests. Teams must use these templates to ensure auditability and accelerate approvals.

- Templates included (and filenames in the template library):
  - Purchase Request Template -> templates/purchase-request-2024.docx
  - Vendor Intake Form -> templates/vendor-intake-2024.pdf
  - Access Request Template -> templates/access-request.json (ITSM importable)
  - Change Ticket Template -> templates/change-ticket.yaml
  - Travel Authorization Form -> templates/travel-authorization-2024.docx

- How to use: Copy the template into your ticket or ticketing tool record. Fill all mandatory fields (indicated in the template). Missing fields will result in auto-reject by the intake automation.

8) Ownership & Escalation (who to contact)
- People Ops: policy maintenance, travel exceptions, employee-facing procurement questions (people-ops@redwood.com).
- Finance: PO issuance, invoicing, and audits (finance-ops@redwood.com).
- Security: vendor security reviews, data classification, incident triage (security@redwood.com).
- Eng-SRE: change windows, emergency rollback decisions (sre-oncall@redwood.com).

9) Metrics & Reporting (SLOs and KPIs)
- Access request SLA: 95% of routine requests processed within 3 business days.
- Change failure rate target: < 0.5% for medium/high-risk changes measured on production anomalies attributed to the change.
- Procurement cycle time: median PO issuance time under 5 business days for approved spend <= $25k.
- Vendor review cadence: medium/high-risk vendors reviewed quarterly; low-risk reviewed annually.

10) Exceptions, Amendments, and Continuous Improvement
- Exceptions: Documented via an Exceptions Request form and approved by policy owner and one executive (People Ops or Finance depending on domain). Exceptions expire within 90 days unless renewed.
- Policy review cadence: This playbook is reviewed annually; interim updates published as needed with changelog.

Appendices
A. Sample change ticket description (plaintext)
- Title: "Canary rollout: quantization-profile v2 for serving-runtime"
- Description: "Rolling canary to 10% of traffic. Monitor p95 latency and model-quality regression tests. Rollback if latency alt +2x or RMSE > 0.05 on validation prompts."

B. Contact matrix (text):
